To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel approach for single-trial classification based on fixation-related potentials FRP that exploits fixation parameters to guide the optimization and that our method outperforms the previous state-of-the-art.

we present a new approach for discriminating single-trial FRPs related to fixations of objects and non-objects in visual search tasks, based on source power decomposition that uses fixation parameters as target variable to guide the optimization, and that our approach outperforms previously reported results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a brain-machine interface BMI based on the fixation-related potential FRP.
the analysis of the human brain activity and eye movements during visual perception.
the analysis of the visual search task.

there is a significant difference in the FRP between fixating objects and non-objects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method allows the classification of neural responses with respect to visual stimuli with high accuracy.

we developed a novel approach for the single-trial classification between fixations on objects and on a plain background, which is based on a decomposition of the EEG source space and a joint analysis of neural and eye-tracking data.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to discriminate between object and non-object fixations by using the FRP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to classify object versus plain background epochs with a high single-trial accuracy by using the FRP.
a joint analysis of neural and eye-tracking data can provide a more powerful tool for decoding visual perception than either data set alone.
it is possible to use the information about eye movements to guide the optimization of source power decomposition in a single trial classification of neural data.
